key_insight: Glioma DNA methylation patterns differ between East Asian and non-Hispanic White cohorts, revealing distinct epigenetic drivers and a CGGA glioblastoma subgroup that often resembles high-grade astrocytoma.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest that ethnicity-aware methylation profiling could improve glioma classification, prognostic assessment, and future personalized treatment strategies.
method: Reclassified glioma subtypes using WHO 2021 CNS tumour criteria.
Analyzed CGGA and TCGA DNA methylation plus transcriptomics data.
Used machine learning classification/clustering to detect methylation patterns and methylation-driven genes.
evidence_signal: In CGGA, 36.7% of glioblastomas (49 cases) were reclassified as high-grade astrocytomas by the model, and CGGA glioblastoma survival was significantly better than TCGA non-Hispanic White glioblastoma survival (p=0.037).
watch_item: Results are retrospective and cohort-specific, so the methylation signatures and gene drivers need external validation before clinical use.
paper_title: Methylation-driven Cancer Genes and Methylation Profiling in Glioma: A Comparative Study between East Asian and non-Hispanic White Populations
